content:
Apple has filed for a preliminary injunction in its ongoing trade secrets lawsuit against OpenAI. Apple says it will suffer "irreparable harm" from the alleged theft of its trade secrets if the injunction isn't granted.

In the filing, Apple says that after it filed the initial lawsuit last month, it sent a letter to OpenAI indicating its intent to "seek preliminary injunctive relief." However, Apple says OpenAI can avoid that step if it agrees to five requests:

  • Stop accessing or using Apple's confidential information
  • Stop any ongoing use or disclosure
  • Preserve all evidence
  • Allow forensic inspection of devices, cloud storage, email, Slack, Teams and other databases
  • Search OpenAI's systems for any of Apple's confidential information

According to Apple, OpenAI has agreed to the first three requests, but the two parties have not reached an agreement on the last two.

As a result, Apple is asking the court to issue a preliminary injunction, asking the judge to immediately bar OpenAI from using or accessing any of Apple's trade secrets, preserve all evidence, allow Apple to conduct forensic inspections of OpenAI's devices and accounts, and return any of Apple's confidential information still in OpenAI's possession.

Apple says:

Apple has also filed a separate motion asking the court to expedite discovery, including obtaining documents early and taking depositions from key OpenAI employees and management out of court.

Apple's filing comes as OpenAI has issued its most detailed public response yet to the lawsuit. In a late-night blog post, OpenAI said the "reckless, combative, and remarkably personal" lawsuit is beneath Apple's reputation as "one of the greatest companies in history."

The injunction hearing is scheduled for October 1, 2026. The full court filings can be viewed below.
